nodes.summary: Let $R$ be a semiring and $Q \in R$. For natural numbers $M$ and $k$ with $M < k$, the Gaussian binomial coefficient $\binom{M}{k}_Q$ is $0$.
nodes.title: Gaussian binomial coefficients vanish when $k > M$

nodes.summary: Let $R$ be a commutative ring and $Q \in R$, and write $P_Q(m) = \prod_{i < m} (1 - Q^{i+1})$ for the finite $Q$-Pochhammer symbol, the product running over the natural numbers $i < m$. For natural numbers $k \le M$, the Gaussian binomial coefficient satisfies $\binom{M}{k}_Q \, P_Q(k) \, P_Q(M - k) = P_Q(M)$.
nodes.title: Product formula for Gaussian binomial coefficients

nodes.summary: Let $R$ be a semiring and $Q \in R$. For every natural number $M$, the Gaussian binomial coefficient $\binom{M}{M}_Q$ equals $1$.
nodes.title: Diagonal Gaussian binomial coefficients

nodes.summary: Let $R$ be a semiring and $Q \in R$. For all natural numbers $M$ and $k$, the Gaussian binomial coefficients satisfy $\binom{M+1}{k+1}_Q = \binom{M}{k}_Q + Q^{k+1} \binom{M}{k+1}_Q$.
nodes.title: $Q$-Pascal recursion for Gaussian binomial coefficients

nodes.summary: Let $R$ be a semiring and $Q \in R$. For every natural number $M$, the Gaussian binomial coefficient $\binom{M}{0}_Q$ equals $1$.
nodes.title: Gaussian binomial coefficients with $k = 0$

nodes.summary: Let $R$ be a semiring and $Q \in R$. For every natural number $k$, the Gaussian binomial coefficient $\binom{0}{k+1}_Q$ equals $0$.
nodes.title: Gaussian binomial coefficients with $M = 0$

nodes.summary: Let $R$ be a semiring and $Q \in R$. For natural numbers $M$ and $k$, the Gaussian binomial coefficient $\binom{M}{k}_Q \in R$ is defined recursively by $\binom{M}{0}_Q = 1$, $\binom{0}{k+1}_Q = 0$ and $\binom{M+1}{k+1}_Q = \binom{M}{k}_Q + Q^{k+1} \binom{M}{k+1}_Q$.
nodes.title: Gaussian binomial coefficient

nodes.title: Ehrenborg–Readdy expansion of the Gaussian coefficient

nodes.summary: Let $R$ be a commutative ring and $Q \in R$, and write $P_Q(m) = \prod_{i < m} (1 - Q^{i+1})$ for the finite $Q$-Pochhammer symbol, the product running over the natural numbers $i < m$. For every natural number $m$, $P_Q(m+1) = P_Q(m) \, (1 - Q^{m+1})$.
nodes.title: Recursion for the finite $Q$-Pochhammer symbol

nodes.summary: Let $R$ be a commutative ring and $Q \in R$. The finite $Q$-Pochhammer symbol $P_Q(m) = \prod_{i < m} (1 - Q^{i+1})$, the product running over the natural numbers $i < m$, satisfies $P_Q(0) = 1$.
nodes.title: The finite $Q$-Pochhammer symbol at $0$

nodes.summary: Let $R$ be a commutative ring and $Q \in R$. For a natural number $m$, the finite $Q$-Pochhammer symbol $P_Q(m) \in R$ is the product $\prod_{i < m} (1 - Q^{i+1})$ of $1 - Q^{i+1}$ over the natural numbers $i < m$.
nodes.title: Finite $Q$-Pochhammer symbol

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
